## Loudness relative to the desktop cues

Interface set mean active RMS: -37.98 dBFS (spread 0.03 dB).

| desktop cue | RMS active | RMS all | interface is quieter by (active) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| done | -40.3 | -41.9 | -2.3 dB |
| request | -41.7 | -43.1 | -3.7 dB |
| attention | -41.8 | -42.7 | -3.9 dB |

Level model. Every `fx_` file carries 6.02 dB of slider headroom: SoundPool volume cannot exceed 1.0, so "100% is twice as loud as the old maximum" has to live in the files. The app plays them at half volume by default (`CueTable.ASSET_BOOST`), which is exactly the old level, and the slider's upper half spends the headroom. The in-app chime copies (`fx_chime_*`) are the desktop chimes plus the same 6.02 dB (checked above); the desktop originals stay untouched for the notification channels.

Why only 2 dB under the chimes: the margin is an audibility floor, not a target. The interface cues are also far shorter than the chimes (tens of milliseconds against several hundred), so at equal RMS they are perceptually quieter still. Measured on active-region RMS.

Promoted desktop auditions (boosted, otherwise untouched) average -36.0 dBFS active RMS, +2.0 dB relative to the interface set.

Scope: peak, onset, clean-end, format and clipping assertions apply to every `fx_` file; the duration, direction, centroid-order and chime-margin assertions apply to the synthesised interface cues only, because the promoted desktop cues are intentionally at desktop level and multi-click.

## Provider cues are told apart

Fingerprint = 12 log-spaced spectral bands (200 Hz to 9.6 kHz), the loudness envelope in 24 slices of the active region (how many hits, how spaced) and the dominant pitch in 8 slices (the contour); distance = mean of the three RMS gaps (24 semitones = 1), minimum allowed 0.2. Closest pairs: cursor / favorites 0.22; devin / other 0.23; claude / antigravity 0.23; hermes / antigravity 0.24.
